title: This Owl Hears a Mouse Under Two Feet of Snow, Then Hovers
subject: great gray owl

scenes.text: An owl hears a vole under two feet of snow. Then it hovers.
The great gray owl hovers over the spot, flapping, for a few seconds.
Snow bends sound, so the squeak seems to come from the wrong place.
Scientists in Manitoba called it an acoustic mirage, and it can be off by about five degrees.
Directly overhead, the error is smallest. The owl pinpoints the vole, then dives through the snow.
The hover isn't hesitation. It's the owl fixing the mirage.

description:
An owl hears a mouse under two feet of snow, then hovers instead of striking.
Snow bends sound into an acoustic mirage, and hovering directly above the spot is how the great gray owl corrects it.
Could you find a sound under two feet of snow?
